prereg.primary_quantity: recovery = 1 - delta_reconstructed / delta_naive, per (organ, sparsity) point; delta_naive read verbatim from d1_pruning.json's block_structured record for that exact (organ, level).
prereg.se_method: paired bootstrap (n_boot=2000, >= 10 required) of delta_reconstructed over sequence resampling on the SAME 24x512 heldout slice D1 used, propagated through the recovery ratio holding delta_naive fixed at its D1 point value (D1's own paired_se on delta_naive is reported alongside per point, not re-bootstrapped jointly -- assumption stated here, not hidden).
prereg.inconclusive_rule: a point's recovery is INCONCLUSIVE iff its [point - 2.0*SE, point + 2.0*SE] interval spans 0.

magnitude_bands_fixed_before_any_result.LARGE: recovery point estimate >= 0.70 AND the lower band bound > 0.5
magnitude_bands_fixed_before_any_result.INCONCLUSIVE: band spans 0, regardless of point estimate

prereg.derivation_note_mask_geometry: D1._struct_axis makes q/k/v/gate/up_proj ROW-structured (whole output neurons zeroed) and o_proj/down_proj COLUMN-structured (whole input features zeroed, same surviving column set S shared across every output row). The row-separable SparseGPT-style solve in this brief only has freedom to act when S varies WITHIN a row's support -- i.e. only for COLUMN-structured organs. For gate_proj (ROW-structured), every kept row already has full support (S = all columns) and every dropped row has none: the closed form is therefore mathematically forced to return exactly W (kept rows) or exactly 0 (dropped rows), independent of H's content. This is stated here, before gate_proj is run, not discovered after.
prereg.scope: gate_proj, o_proj, down_proj (one MLP-expansion/ROW-structured, one attn-output/COLUMN-structured, one MLP-contraction/COLUMN-structured) at sparsity {0.25, 0.50, 0.75}. 0.90 excluded per brief (quantisation artefact struck for k/v_proj in D1; not requested for these three organs anyway).
prereg.control3_control4_scope_decision: Hessian ablation (control 3) and leakage control (control 4) are run on down_proj@0.5 only, a time-budget decision stated up front: down_proj is the larger and only-interesting-case-among-the-two COLUMN-structured organs tested (in_features=8960 vs o_proj's 1536), so it is the instance the reconstruction mechanism is most staked on. o_proj's sweep numbers stand on real-H only and are NOT independently ablated -- flagged in the report.

calib_eval_disjointness.assertion: calib and heldout are two DIFFERENT physical corpus files (benchmarks/donor_adaptation/density/corpus/{calib,heldout}.txt), built by splitting the globally-shuffled chunk list in half BEFORE either slice is drawn (build_calib.py) -- disjoint by construction, and their distinct sha256 hashes are asserted equal to the manifest's own record here, not merely assumed.

identity.gate_proj_note: ROW-structured: at mask=0% no rows are zeroed, no solve is invoked at all (see reconstruct_row_axis_level) -- weight deviation is exactly 0 by construction, not run as a separate eval.
identity.o_proj_note: Not separately measured (time budget): same COLUMN-structured solve as down_proj, same S=full-set-at-0%-mask argument; down_proj is the larger case and stands as the representative check.

ABORTED_BY_PRINCIPAL.reason: Control 1 (identity, mask=0%) failed: delta=+0.34921 BPB, max_abs_weight_deviation=0.6545, fired=false. Two causes identified: (1) regularisation asymmetry -- the solve used H[S,S]+lambda*I as the system matrix but the UNregularised H[:,S] on the right-hand side, so even at S=full the closed form computes W @ H @ (H+lambda*I)^-1 != W. (2) the calibration set was far too small for down_proj (d_ffn=8960): T=4096 tokens gives rank(H) <= 4096, so rank(H)/N = 4096/8960 = 0.457 < 0.5, the Failure Mode 1 threshold from the joint-solver dossier adjudication -- H[S,S] submatrices at the tested sparsity levels are singular/near-singular and the solve is dominated by the regulariser rather than the data.
ABORTED_BY_PRINCIPAL.action: Run aborted. Fix required: (1) regularise H once up front (H_reg = H + lambda*I) and use H_reg consistently on BOTH the system matrix and the right-hand side (SparseGPT convention) -- this makes the S=full identity case algebraically exact regardless of H rank. (2) raise the calibration token count so rank(H)/N is comfortably above 0.5 for down_proj, the widest organ tested. (3) add rank(H)/N as a reported diagnostic computed BEFORE every solve, with an automatic abort below 0.5.

fixes_applied: Cause 1 (regularisation asymmetry, the bug): reconstruct_row now builds H_reg = H + lambda*I ONCE over the full DxD matrix and uses that SAME H_reg on both the system matrix and the right-hand side (SparseGPT convention), instead of regularising only the system matrix while leaving the right-hand side on the unregularised H. Confirmed on synthetic data (T=15 < D=40, deliberately rank-deficient): identity-control weight deviation is now exactly 0.0 (was 0.65 before the fix).
